Run WF-02 Step 3b's gate: (a) every REQ-002 acceptance criterion has a verification case; (b) no TODO; (c) each case precise enough to run without judgment. result.summary: Independently re-verified docs/agents/test-specs/REQ-002.md against WF-02 Step 3b's gate: (a) every AC (1-6) has a precise, runnable case, (b) no TODO found, (c) each case is precise enough to run without judgment. Ran my own node scripts against messages/ru.json and messages/uz.json (not TEST-DESIGNER's) and recomputed the identical-value-pair list from scratch: got the exact same 21 keys, exact same values, 0 empty uz values, identical key sets (177/177) between locales. Read every one of the 21 keys' actual ru/uz values myself and judged each on its own merits: all 21 are genuinely non-translatable (event/date codes, country/org-role labels rendered as short badges, a Telegram handle, a hashtag, a URL, a proper product/event name, an NPS acronym, a metric string) -- none is a missed translation. Cross-checked against sibling keys in the same objects (Events.talk1Who/Topic/Desc, Team.team1Desc) to confirm real prose in those same sections IS translated, proving the 21 exceptions aren't a blanket miss. Found strong corroborating evidence: Hero.pillTajikistan/pillKyrgyzstan contain '<COUNTRY> -- SCORO' in ru and are correctly translated to '<COUNTRY> -- TEZDA' in uz, while pillKazakhstan/pillUzbekistan (pure country-name pills with no Russian-specific content) are correctly left identical -- showing the translator handled this exact key family attentively rather than blanket-copying. Re-ran the Cyrillic scan (0 matches) and a corrected emoji scan (0 matches) directly -- both match the spec's expected output exactly. Verified the arrow-exclusion reasoning: the same 10 arrow (U+2192) characters across the same 8 keys exist identically in ru.json as a UI nav affordance, correctly outside the scanned emoji blocks -- confirmed sound, though noted the spec's supporting prose says '9 occurrences' when it is actually 10 characters across 8 keys (Doors.door3Body contains two arrows) -- a cosmetic inaccuracy in explanatory text only, not in the runnable check or its expected output, so not a gate failure. Also independently re-ran npm run build: clean, matches AC5's expected output exactly (Compiled successfully, TypeScript finished with no errors, route table includes /[locale] and Proxy Middleware). Verified AC3's CSS line (globals.css:152, unconditional text-transform:uppercase) and the 8 expected lowercase status values exactly as claimed. No coverage gaps, no TODOs, no ambiguity requiring judgment calls at run time.
issues: Minor: AC4b's supporting prose states the arrow character appears '9 times' in uz.json; the actual count is 10 characters across 8 keys (Doors.door3Body contains two arrows: 'Contributor → committer → maintainer'). This does not affect the runnable check (regex and expected output are correct) -- informational only, no rework required.
